muc.title: One rule for the whole family
muc.text: Fake voices, fake faces, fake celebrities, fake messages. Mark asks: is there a simple way to keep the whole family safe?

muc.title: A secret word
muc.text: Bit suggests: set up a family password. A secret word everyone in the family knows, never texted or posted online.

muc.title: Ask when money comes up
muc.text: If someone calls asking for money urgently, no matter how much the voice or face looks like family, ask for the password. Wrong answer or hesitation? Hang up right away.

muc.title: Easy to remember, hard to guess
muc.text: Pick a phrase that's easy to remember but hard to guess. Don't use pet names or birthdays, because those are often already online.

muc.title: Four safety rules
muc.text: Plus three more rules from this series: call back on the saved number, never read out a one-time code to anyone, and money is never urgent.

muc.title: Talk in person
muc.text: Older people are targeted most. Talk with your grandparents and parents in person, and practice a fake call so they get used to it.

muc.title: Pick it over dinner
muc.text: Tonight, pick your family password over dinner, and remind everyone never to write it online.
